text.en:
One peanut chikki bar is shared equally among 4 friends, then two bars among 3!
"Fractions tell us each fair share cleanly," said Meera.

A fraction represents equal parts of a single whole or a collection—such as 1/2 (one half), 1/4 (one quarter) and 3/4 (three quarters). Every part MUST be equal in size!
Written as a/b, the bottom number is the Denominator—showing how many equal parts make one whole.
The top number is the Numerator—counting how many of those equal parts we take. On a number line between 0 and 1, fractions show exact positions between whole numbers.
When one chikki bar or paratha isn't divided into whole bars, Fractions let us name every fair share accurately.

board.text: Fractions name fair parts of a whole

text.en: Rule number one: parts MUST be equal! Cutting a roti unevenly does not give true halves.
Split one bar into 2 equal pieces: each piece is 1/2 (one half). Split into 4 equal pieces: each piece is 1/4 (one quarter).
Take 3 of those 4 equal quarters and you hold 3/4 (three quarters).

board.text: 3/4 = three out of four equal parts

text.en: Look at the two numbers in 3/4: the bottom number 4 is the Denominator—telling how many equal parts make 1 whole.
The top number 3 is the Numerator—telling how many of those parts we are counting.
What does 4/4 equal? All 4 quarters together rebuild 1 whole! And 5/4 gives 1 whole plus 1/4 more—an improper/mixed fraction 1¼.
Place fractions on a number line: split the gap from 0 to 1 into denominator pieces, then step numerator steps right!
Spot Equivalent Fractions: half a bar (1/2) equals 2/4 and 3/6—different cuts, exact same amount!
So whenever you read a/b, read 'a pieces out of b equal pieces making one whole'!

board.text: Read a/b = a parts of b equal wholes

problem.en: Three parathas are shared equally among 4 friends. How much does each friend get, and what are the numerator and denominator?

text.en: Split each of the 3 parathas into 4 equal quarters.

why.en: Friends take 1 quarter from each paratha -> 3 quarters total per friend.
Each friend gets 3/4 of a paratha.
Numerator = 3 (pieces taken), Denominator = 4 (equal parts per whole paratha).

prompt.en: Is 1/4 larger than 1/2 because 4 is larger than 2?

requiredIdeas.en: No! Sharing 1 bar among 4 gives smaller pieces than sharing among 2.

points.en: Fraction = equal parts of a whole.
Equivalent fractions like 1/2 = 2/4 name the same size.
